content: 1. The antibiotic chloramphenicol reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is relevant only for oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Cefadroxil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by modifying the intestinal flora. This interaction applies exclusively to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is minimal, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Cefazolin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral hormonal forms. The likelihood of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Cefdinir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by modifying the intestinal flora. This interaction pertains only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concurrent use. 7. Ceftibuten reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by modifying the intestinal flora. This interaction applies exclusively to oral hormonal forms. The likelihood of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Cefuroxime decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction pertains only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is minimal, but caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Additionally, cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate through the same mechanism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary when co-administered with cenobamate. 14. Cephalexin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Clobazam reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished when used concurrently. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 16. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 18. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Clarithromycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by modifying the intestinal flora. This interaction pertains only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is minimal, but therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 20. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies exclusively to oral hormonal forms. The likelihood of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 22. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of cyclosporine through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 24. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates; dose reduction of BCRP substrates should be considered based on prescribing information. 25. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered, and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 26. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have serious or life-threatening effects at elevated plasma concentrations. 28. Encorafenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments of these substrates. 29. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by modifying the intestinal flora. This interaction pertains only to oral hormonal forms. The likelihood of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are necessary. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 31. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies exclusively to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is minimal, but caution and monitoring are advised. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 32. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by modifying the intestinal flora. This interaction pertains only to oral hormonal forms. The likelihood of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are necessary. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 33. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, and the use of a non-hormonal contraceptive is recommended. 34. Exenatide injectable solution may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance when used with oral contraceptives. Additionally, exenatide slows gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 35. Exenatide injectable suspension may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance when used with oral contraceptives. Additionally, exenatide slows gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 36. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 37. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 38. Iloperidone increases the levels of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 39. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Fostemsavir inhibits BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates when co-administered with fostemsavir. Do not exceed an ethinyl estradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 43. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 45. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of green tea by decreasing its elimination. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may reduce the effects of hemin. 47. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Estrogens, when administered in large systemic doses, may render tissues partially resistant to the action of hyaluronidase. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects.
